outcome: umbilical artery N-terminal proBrain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels
cohort: 140 pregnant women who delivered by cesarean section between 37 and 40 weeks of gestation, divided into an elective cesarean group (control) and a cesarean due to fetal distress group (study).
finding: Umbilical artery NT-proBNP levels were significantly higher in fetuses delivered by cesarean section due to fetal distress compared to those delivered by elective cesarean section, suggesting NT-proBNP as a marker for fetal distress.
cross-section timing: At the time of delivery for term pregnancies (37-40 weeks gestation)
